section: Sustainable development - meaning, nature, scope and components
subsections: Judicial recognition in India - landmark cases

accepted.s: Which landmark judgment recognised sustainable development, the precautionary principle and the polluter-pays principle as part of Indian environmental law?
o: Indian Council for Enviro-Legal Action v. Union of India
Vellore Citizens' Welfare Forum v. Union of India
Narmada Bachao Andolan v. Union of India
accepted.x: Vellore Citizens' Welfare Forum v. Union of India (1996) recognised sustainable development, the precautionary principle and the polluter-pays principle in Indian environmental law.
accepted.tq: Identify the landmark judgment from the specific principles associated with it.
accepted.sec: Judicial recognition in India - landmark cases

accepted.s:
With reference to environmental jurisprudence in India, consider the following statements:
1. The polluter-pays principle was recognised in Indian Council for Enviro-Legal Action v. Union of India.
2. The public trust doctrine was recognised in M.C. Mehta v. Kamal Nath.
3. The precautionary principle was recognised in Vellore Citizens' Welfare Forum v. Union of India.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The 1996 Indian Council case affirmed polluter pays, the 1997 Kamal Nath case recognised the public trust doctrine, and the 1996 Vellore case recognised the precautionary principle.
accepted.tq: Match each case with its distinctive environmental-law principle.
accepted.sec: Judicial recognition in India - landmark cases

accepted.s:
The constitutional foundation for environmental protection in India includes which of the following provisions?
1. Article 21
2. Article 48A
3. Article 51A(g)
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Articles 21, 48A and 51A(g) together constitute the constitutional base identified for environmental protection and sustainable development in India.
accepted.tq: Use the complete constitutional grouping rather than selecting only one category of provision.
accepted.sec: Judicial recognition in India - landmark cases

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the National Green Tribunal (NGT):
1. It is a statutory body established under the NGT Act, 2010.
2. It is a constitutional body created directly by the Constitution of India.
3. Its headquarters is at New Delhi.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The NGT is a statutory body under the NGT Act, 2010, and its headquarters is at New Delhi. It is not a constitutional body.
accepted.tq: Spot the wrong institutional classification by contrasting statutory and constitutional bodies.
accepted.sec: Judicial recognition in India - landmark cases

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT a bench location of the National Green Tribunal mentioned in the institutional arrangement?
accepted.x: The NGT benches mentioned are at Bhopal, Pune, Kolkata and Chennai. Hyderabad is not included in this list.
accepted.tq: Find the location that does not belong to the stated list of NGT benches.
accepted.sec: Judicial recognition in India - landmark cases

accepted.s: The National Green Tribunal is required to apply which combination of principles while adjudicating environmental cases?
o: Sustainable development, precautionary principle and polluter-pays principle
Public trust doctrine, absolute liability and eminent domain
Common but differentiated responsibilities, prior appropriation and res judicata
Inter-generational equity, federal supremacy and parliamentary privilege
accepted.x: The NGT must apply the principles of sustainable development, precautionary action and polluter pays.
accepted.tq: Select the complete statutory-principle combination rather than a partly related doctrine.
accepted.sec: Judicial recognition in India - landmark cases

accepted.s: The principal aim of the Swarna Andhra @2047 vision is to make Andhra Pradesh a:
o: Healthy, Digital and Fully Urban state by 2047
Carbon-neutral, Industrial and Export-oriented state by 2035
Wealthy, Nuclear and Self-sufficient state by 2030
Wealthy, Healthy and Happy state by 2047
accepted.x: Swarna Andhra @2047 aims to make Andhra Pradesh a “Wealthy, Healthy and Happy” state by 2047.
accepted.tq: Recall the exact official formulation of the vision rather than substituting related development objectives.

accepted.s: Swarna Andhra @2047 is aligned with which of the following national visions?
accepted.x: The Swarna Andhra @2047 vision is aligned with Viksit Bharat @2047.
accepted.tq: Use the matching year and title to identify the aligned national vision.

accepted.s: Which one of the following is identified as a strategic pillar of the Swarna Andhra @2047 vision?
accepted.x: Sustainability and Climate Resilience is one of the strategic pillars of Swarna Andhra @2047.
accepted.tq: Choose the formally stated strategic pillar instead of an opposite or unlisted policy direction.

accepted.s: Which set of measures is associated with the Sustainability and Climate Resilience pillar of Swarna Andhra @2047?
o: Renewable energy, green mobility and sustainable urban planning
Coal expansion, private transport and dispersed urbanisation
Nuclear energy, rural depopulation and industrial zoning
River diversion, road widening and conventional urban planning
accepted.x: The pillar includes renewable energy, green mobility and sustainable urban planning.
accepted.tq: Select the option containing the complete set of measures linked to the pillar.

accepted.s: The sustainability framework of Swarna Andhra @2047 is guided by the:
accepted.x: The sustainability framework is guided by Ten Sutras under APSES 2024-25.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the exact number and source framework associated with the vision.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding renewable energy under the Swarna Andhra @2047 vision:
1. Its contribution is approximately 30% at present.
2. The target is to increase the contribution to more than 75% by 2047.
3. The target is to keep the contribution below 50% by 2047.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Renewable energy contributes approximately 30% currently, with a target of more than 75% by 2047. Statement 3 reverses the stated target and is false.
accepted.tq: Compare the present level with the long-term target and reject the reversed trend.

accepted.s: The green-cover targets associated with Swarna Andhra @2047 are:
accepted.x: The stated green-cover targets are 37% by 2030 and 50% by 2047.
accepted.tq: Keep the two target years paired with their correct percentages.

accepted.s: The AP-UN-Habitat Memorandum of Understanding of July 2026 envisages establishment of a Centre of Excellence for Urban Affairs at:
accepted.x: The July 2026 AP-UN-Habitat MoU envisages a Centre of Excellence for Urban Affairs in Amaravati.
accepted.tq: Identify the location directly associated with the named institutional initiative.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the AP-UN-Habitat MoU of July 2026:
1. It relates to climate-resilient cities.
2. It is connected with Sustainable Development Goal 11.
3. It proposes a Centre of Excellence for Urban Affairs in Amaravati.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The MoU covers climate-resilient cities, is connected with SDG 11, and provides for a Centre of Excellence for Urban Affairs in Amaravati.
accepted.tq: Test several closely related features of the same current-affairs agreement.

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes UN-Habitat?
o: It was set up in 1992 and has its headquarters at Amaravati.
It was set up in 1987 and has its headquarters at New Delhi.
It was set up in 1978 and has its headquarters at Nairobi.
It was set up in 1972 and has its headquarters at Geneva.
accepted.x: UN-Habitat was set up in 1978 and is headquartered at Nairobi.
accepted.tq: Discriminate the organisation by checking both its establishment year and headquarters.

accepted.s: Which group of themes has been identified as the most frequently asked area in this sustainability-related context?
o: Stockholm, Rio, Brundtland and the Sustainable Development Goals
Wetlands, mangroves, deserts and coral reefs
Ozone depletion, acid rain, nuclear energy and biotechnology
accepted.x: The most frequently asked themes are Stockholm, Rio, the Brundtland Commission and the Sustainable Development Goals.
accepted.tq: Recognise the recurring international sustainability milestones as a thematic group.

accepted.s: The Sustainable Development Report (SDR) 2025 placed India at which rank?
accepted.x: India was ranked 99th in the Sustainable Development Report 2025.
accepted.tq: Recall the specific rank and distinguish it from nearby numerical distractors.

accepted.s: Which of the following is cited as a sustainability model in Andhra Pradesh through APFDC?
accepted.x: APFDC is cited as a sustainability model involving 49,743 hectares of plantations.
accepted.tq: Identify the exact area figure associated with the state sustainability model.

accepted.s: APNGC Eco-Clubs are cited in the context of:
accepted.x: APNGC Eco-Clubs are cited as a sustainability model in Andhra Pradesh.
accepted.tq: Link the named state initiative with its stated sustainability function.

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly represents the first occurrence and the first definition associated with sustainable development in the stated international chronology?
accepted.x: The first Earth Summit was held at Rio in 1992, while the first definition is associated with the Brundtland Commission in 1987.
accepted.tq: Separate the event from the definition and pair each with its correct year.
